leg: Lane 2 — Homebound exits for 5 pax (Nov 1-3, 2026): Romania (OTP/CLJ), Iberia (LIS/MAD), the Dublin baseline re-priced with positioning, and Zagreb

summary: Lane 2 verdict: the Dublin anchor is broken and stays broken. Priced honestly with positioning at true 5-pax rates (live Ryanair API), the best Dublin path is Krakow->DUB Nov 1 ($347/5, lands 08:50) + EI61 (81,250 Avios + $973) = $1,320 cash + 81k Avios, home Nov 1 — but that only ties, not beats, a Flying Blue feeder award home from Krakow itself (~137.5k MR + ~$650, one ticket, no cutover risk); from Budapest or Prague the Dublin detour forces Nov 3 arrival and is strictly worse. Romania's headline: the Flying Blue OTP->AMS->SFO feeder play (~125-150k MR + ~$650 for all five) is the strongest points exit found in this lane, with HiSky OTP->JFK (2x weekly from Oct 25, Monday Nov 2 likely, ~$2,250 all-in incl. JFK-SFO) as a serviceable cash fallback and ~$2,750 for conventional one-stops. Lisbon works too: TAP LIS-SFO verified operating through winter (~3-4x/wk, ~$2,700/5 cash) AND Lisbon supports the same FB feeder trick — making it points-equal to Bucharest. Madrid is impaired (MAD-SFO nonstop almost certainly ends late Oct; MAD->LAX at ~24k Avios pp works but positioning from DBV to Iberia is unsolved). Zagreb is the weakest exit: cash-only ~$3,100/5 with no FB feeder in winter. Net ranking for the destination decision: Krakow and Bucharest/Romania exit cheapest (points), Lisbon close behind, Dublin only as a points-conservation play from Krakow, Zagreb needs an escape hop.
caveats: Live-verified at 5 pax: all Ryanair positioning fares (KRK/BUD/PRG->DUB, farfnd v4, 2026-08-02) and prior-pass items (EI61 award, DBV matrix, DBV->ZAG). NOT live-verified: (1) Flying Blue award space/pricing for 5 on specific Nov dates — 25-30k saver is historical-typical and FB is dynamic; the feeder-included pricing mechanism was verified in a prior pass but current levels must be checked on klm.com before committing; (2) HiSky's exact early-Nov op days (NW26 confirmed 2x weekly from Oct 25; Mon/Wed vs Mon/Fri unresolved) and its ~290 EUR pp fare; (3) TAP LIS-SFO exact Nov 1-2 op days (winter operation itself is verified); (4) Iberia MAD-SFO end-of-season exact date (assumed ended by Nov 1) and Iberia award space for 5; (5) all cash one-stop figures (OTP/ZAG/LIS ~$2,700-3,100) are aggregator-estimates from search snippets, not live 5-pax itinerary quotes — Google Flights, skiplagged, HiSky and flightsfrom all blocked programmatic access this session. Currency conversions at 2026-08-02 rates (PLN 3.735, HUF 315.3, CZK 20.99/USD). Same-day KRK->DUB->EI61 is a separate-ticket connection (~4h buffer) — a Ryanair delay forfeits the award; an Oct 31 position ($513/5 + hotel) de-risks it.

summary: All 20 city/date cells quoted LIVE at true 5-pax pricing on Google Flights (headless, tfs URLs; raw JSON saved to data/raw/lane1-flights/). CASH LADDER (total for five): PRAGUE $2,365 (BA via LHR, Nov 1 — cheapest on the board, but avoid Nov 2's $4,153 spike) < BUDAPEST $2,887 (BA, Oct 31/Nov 3) < WARSAW $3,028 (SAS via CPH nonstop-to-SFO, Nov 1, fastest at 13h35) < VIENNA $3,161 (BA, Nov 2/3) < KRAKOW $3,379 (SAS via CPH, Nov 2/3). Schedule facts verified: LOT WAW-SFO is summer-seasonal (no winter 2026/27 service — do not plan on it); LOT KRK-ORD winter service is Mondays-only historically and never surfaced in a bookable 5-pax combo; Iberia MAD-SFO is also summer-seasonal, killing the low-fee Avios-via-MAD play; Austrian/Lufthansa Star options price $7,300+ for five — never competitive. AWARD: the Flying Blue O&D mechanic is publicly confirmed — any lane-1 city ->AMS/CDG->SFO prices at the transatlantic level with the feeder FREE. Economy saver floor is now 25,000/pp (125,000 MR + ~$600 fees for five), and the AUGUST PROMO gives KLM PREMIUM ECONOMY Europe<->SFO at 30,000/pp (150,000 MR for five in a premium cabin, book by Aug 31, travel window covers Nov 1-3). Against the 525k MR pool either fits with 375k+ to spare, and both crush the dead Dublin baseline (81,250 Avios + $973 + a $705 Oct-25-only Ryanair feeder). Decision shape: if the destination is Prague, pay cash ($2,365 makes the econ award only ~1.4 cpp); anywhere else, the FB award wins IF five saver/promo seats verify — that check is login-gated and must happen BEFORE any irreversible MR transfer, because Flying Blue reprices the whole party ~5x when fewer than 5 saver seats exist.
caveats: (1) Cash quotes are live Google Flights totals for 4 adults + 1 child (airlines price the 16yo and 13yo as adults, the 8yo as child) pulled 2026-08-02; fares move — the PRG Nov 2 spike shows cheap buckets already selling through. (2) Award SPACE for 5 seats is UNVERIFIED — all award rows are floor/promo levels with mechanics confirmed publicly; the seats.aero/logged-in check is the mandatory gate, and FB's whole-party flex repricing is the failure mode. FB fee figures (~$110-140/pp via AMS) are typical, not quoted. (3) The 30k PE promo requires BOOKING BY AUG 31 2026 — that is 29 days away and forces the destination decision if the premium-economy play is wanted. (4) LOT winter 2026/27 timetable (post Oct 25) is not fully published; WAW-SFO/KRK-ORD conclusions rest on the announced summer-seasonal pattern plus their absence from live Nov results. (5) Positioning from Dubrovnik is NOT included in any price_usd above: add $232/5 (KRK, direct), $295/5 (VIE, to Nov 1), or VIE/KRK + ground for PRG/BUD/WAW. (6) BA/Iberia award rows are quantified estimates for comparison, not live quotes; both are dominated and were not priced to the dollar.

summary: WINNER: KRAKOW. Memory-per-dollar arithmetic (score / effective-$k, MR valued at the 1.54cpp project floor): Krakow 8/$5,507=1.45 > Prague 7.5/$5,410=1.39 > Transylvania 8.5/$6,370=1.33 > Budapest 7/$5,570=1.26 > Slovenia 7.5/$6,862=1.09 > Lisbon 7/$6,975=1.00. Krakow wins BOTH halves of Jarred's brief: top-tier memory (Wieliczka underground, Zakopane thermal parks, and the family standing in the Nov 1 All Saints candle-sea the night before they fly — a calendar accident this trip's dates hand them for free) AND the cheapest, most-verified logistics on the board — the only destination with a direct, live-quoted, whole-window feeder ($232/5 Ryanair DBV->KRK, Oct 25) and three independent ways home. HOW THEY GET HOME: Ryanair DBV->KRK Oct 25 ($232 cash, book now); then Mon Nov 2, one Flying Blue award ticket KRK->AMS->SFO for all five — 125,000 Amex MR (5x25k economy saver, KRK-AMS Cityhopper leg FREE under the verified O&D mechanic) + ~$600 fees, arriving SFO Nov 2 — or 150,000 MR for KLM PREMIUM ECONOMY under the August promo (book by Aug 31). Total trip cash ~$3,582 + 125k MR, leaving 400k MR in the pool. Fallbacks from the same city if award space fails: SAS cash KRK->CPH->SFO Nov 2 $3,379 (live-confirmed), or the Dublin conserve play. WHAT THE FREED EXIT CHANGED: everything. The old Dublin path from Krakow costs $1,320 cash + 81,250 Avios with three flights and a separate-ticket transatlantic cutover; the FB award costs $600 cash + 125,000 MR on ONE ticket — $720 less cash, no cutover risk, near-identical economic value ($2,525 vs $2,571 effective), and the PE promo turns it into a premium cabin for five at a level Dublin can never touch. Dublin survives only as a points-conservation fallback; it anchors nothing. Prague meanwhile emerged as the cheapest pure-cash exit ever found ($2,365/5 live) and is the designated no-points Plan B if FB space fails. LIVE-QUOTED: all DBV feeders, all lane-1 cash exits, all Ryanair Dublin positioning. ESTIMATED: every daily burn, activity add-on, ground/train leg, and ALL Flying Blue award space. THE ONE THING TO VERIFY BEFORE ANY BOOKING: five saver/promo seats on KRK->AMS->SFO for Nov 2 (or Nov 1/3), checked logged-in on klm.com/flyingblue BEFORE transferring a single MR — transfers are irreversible and Flying Blue reprices the ENTIRE party ~5x to flex if even one of the five saver seats is missing. Run that check this week: the 30k PE promo dies Aug 31, 29 days out.
caveats: (1) FB award rows are mechanics-verified but SPACE-unverified; the logged-in 5-seat check is the gate for the winner, and SAS $3,379 cash (live) is the confirmed fallback that caps downside — Krakow wins under either exit (cash-exit Krakow total $6,361 all-cash still ranks #2, 1.26/k, behind only Prague). (2) Daily burns ($350/day Central Europe, $400 Slovenia, $500 Lisbon) and activity/car/train add-ons are prior-research estimates, not quotes; a +/-$50/day swing moves totals ~$350 but does not reorder the top 3 (Krakow's lead over Prague is 0.06/k — close; Prague is a legitimate winner if Jarred rejects the award-risk entirely). (3) Transylvania's positioning (~$595) was never priced at 5 pax — if a real quote comes back under ~$450 AND FB space at OTP verifies, it closes to ~1.36/k, still #3 but within argument range of its 8.5 memory score. (4) MR valued at 1.54cpp per the project floor; at a lower personal valuation the all-cash Prague plan gains ground. (5) Fares move: PRG Nov 2 already spiked to $4,153, so the cheap cells (PRG Nov 1, KRK $232 feeder) should be locked within days of the destination decision. (6) Ryanair feeder and FB award are separate tickets — the Oct 25 feeder is 7 days before the exit, so no misconnect risk, but Ryanair bag rules apply to a family of 5 (add ~$150-250 for checked bags, not included above, applies equally to all Ryanair-fed plans).
